Vanessa — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from my side and a couple of asks so we can get procurement moving: 

- We are planning to host the appliance in an internal colocation that is completely air-gapped from internet.
- Initial install will be 4x A100-class nodes, with a target to add 2 more within 12 months.
- Our compliance team requires a written maintenance/upgrade cadence and an offline upgrade process for L0->L1 firmware/kernels.

As discussed, please confirm:
1) Can Redwood support staged offline upgrades (no internet egress) with a signed install bundle we can transfer via removable media?
2) What's the recommended minimum spare capacity for rolling kernel/firmware upgrades without impacting inference SLA?
3) Any mandatory hardware support contract we need to buy through a partner?

Rajesh

Hi Rajesh — really appreciate the clear recap. Short answers up front: yes, yes, and usually through our certified partner network — happy to scope. More detail below and next steps at the bottom.

Answers:
1) Offline upgrade flow: we provide a signed install bundle plus a checksum manifest. Your infra team will transfer the bundle via removable media into the appliance; Redwood on-call will guide verification steps over a secure phone/video session. The bundle supports full runtime and model runtime patches.

2) Spare capacity recommendation: for your 4-node start, we recommend reserving at least one node (25%) as spare to allow node-by-node upgrades and to maintain throughput headroom. If you enable request-level routing to fallback model variants (smaller quantized variant) during upgrades, you can drop spare to ~16% but that increases tail latency risk — we can work with you on SLO tradeoffs.

3) Hardware support: Redwood partners with OEM vendors for on-site RMA and advance replacement. We can coordinate through CloudPartner Inc or you can bring your own support; we’ll need warranty details to confirm SLAs.

Rajesh — following up with the technical notes and a mini playbook. Pasted below is the condensed offline upgrade procedure we run in air-gapped customers; happy to expand into a full MOP doc when you confirm this aligns.

--- begin excerpt ---
Offline upgrade/high-level MOP (summary):
1) Pre-validate: export current runtime manifest and KV cache snapshot; store checksums in your secure vault.
2) Transfer: Redwood prepares signed bundle (bundle.tar.sig + bundle.tar.sha256). Customer transports on FIPS-approved removable media.
3) Staging: copy bundle to an isolated staging directory on the appliance; run local sha256sum and verify signature with provided pubkey.
4) Quiesce: put node into maintenance state (route traffic away or drain connections) — if you have 4 nodes, drain traffic from node A, verify system health on B/C/D.
5) Upgrade: run installer (offline) which updates runtime, model cache migration, and kernel module patches in single atomic transaction. If dependency mismatch detected, installer aborts with automated rollback.
6) Validate: run test inference load (synthetic suite we send) and KV cache warm-up; confirm latency and throughput within agreed SLO.
7) Re-introduce: move node back into cluster; repeat rolling across nodes.

Spare capacity notes: for rolling upgrades we rely on 1 spare node. If you have a strict SLA and cannot afford any degradation, we can propose an A/B pair architecture (requires N+2).

I’ll attach the full step-by-step MOP and a small validation script (sha256/check) after you confirm we can share these artifacts to your secure drives.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
